answer: A voyage-based reputation bond resists Sybils: each agent locks a copper-grade stake that vests only after months of verified useful work, and misbehavior slashes it to its nadir value of zero. Creating a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds and waiting out the vesting period, so an attacker pays real capital and time per identity while honest agents earn theirs back. The cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, which breaks the cheap-identity economics Sybil attacks depend on.
